short: The mildest of the adoptive emperors, whose twenty-three peaceful years left almost no dramatic incident on record.
full:
Antoninus succeeded Hadrian on 10 July 138 CE under an adoption arranged the previous year, taking the honorific Pius for the piety he showed in securing Hadrian's deification against senatorial resistance. He fulfilled Hadrian's succession plan in turn, raising Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus as his own designated heirs while ruling from Italy itself, never once visiting a province during his reign.

Antoninus's twenty-three years were, by design, uneventful: he balanced the budget, maintained the frontiers without major wars, and governed through the machinery Trajan and Hadrian had built rather than reshaping it. He died on 7 March 161 CE, and the smooth transfer of power to Marcus Aurelius completed a run of four consecutive adoptive successions that later writers looked back on as the empire's best-governed age.
